To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the signal attenuation and pulse broadening in FSOC are strongly affected by cloud properties, such as the cloud optical thickness, the cloud droplet size and number, and the cloud droplet shape; (ii) the correlation between spatial and temporal dispersion is very strong, and the correlation between angular and temporal dispersion is weak; (iii) the pulse broadening and energy loss are strongly affected by the receiver aperture size, the FOV, and the position of receiver relative to the transmitter.

the signal characteristics of a free space optical communication (FSOC) system operating as a ground-air link through clouds are affected by cloud properties, receiver aperture size, and receiver field-of-view (FoV).
the dispersion of the transmitted beam is a strong function of receiver aperture size and FOV, and the position of receiver relative to the transmitter optical axis.
